title: Linkability of student submissions to other student data
description: Student ID, course, and submission timestamp in this flow can be linked to other student records (grades, attendance, previous submissions) to create comprehensive student profiles, potentially revealing patterns about study habits, performance trends, and personal circumstances.
assumptions: System maintains multiple data stores with student information that can be cross-referenced

title: Direct identifiability of student from submission data
description: Student ID is explicitly transmitted in the assignment submission, making the student directly identifiable. Combined with course and timestamp, this creates a clear identity trail for each submission.
assumptions: Student ID is a unique identifier that can be used to identify the individual student

title: Unauthorized disclosure of assignment content during transmission
description: Assignment work file, student ID, course information, and submission timestamp could be intercepted during transmission if the connection between student and Grades Portal is not properly secured (e.g., missing TLS/SSL encryption).
assumptions: Data is transmitted over network that could be vulnerable to interception

title: Data aggregation across multiple submissions
description: Multiple assignment submissions from the same student can be aggregated to analyze performance patterns, submission timing habits, and learning behaviors, potentially revealing sensitive information about the student's academic struggles or personal circumstances.
assumptions: System stores historical submission data that can be aggregated and analyzed

title: Unintended recipients of submission data
description: Assignment data may be forwarded to unintended recipients such as analytics services, logging systems, third-party integrations, or backup systems without the student's explicit knowledge or consent.
assumptions: System may have integrations with external services or logging mechanisms

title: Student identifier transmitted in grading request
description: The flow transmits student ID as part of submission and grading requests, containing a unique reference to the identity of the data subject. This enables identification of individual students throughout the grading process.
assumptions: Student ID is a unique identifier that can be used to identify individual students

title: Processing of identified student data
description: The portal requests and processes identified student data (student ID, course, file reference) when routing to the assignment & grading service, creating privacy exposure through identified data processing.
assumptions: The system processes data that can be linked to specific students

title: Non-repudiation of student submission requests
description: The flow includes requesting role information that creates evidence of student involvement in submission requests. Students may be unable to deny their participation in the grading process based on this transmitted data.
assumptions: Requesting role data can be used to attribute actions to specific individuals
uncertainty_note: Tree node Nr.1.1 is inferred from general non-repudiation threat patterns; exact node may vary by threat tree version

title: Direct Identifiability of Students
description: The flow transmits student ID along with assignment files, enabling direct identification of individual students. This personal identifier is stored in the Assignment Store, creating a persistent link between students and their submissions.
assumptions: Student ID is a unique personal identifier that can be used to identify individuals

title: Linkability Across Student Data
description: Student ID, course, and submission time in this flow can be linked with other student data in the system (e.g., grades, attendance, other assignments), enabling comprehensive profiling of student activities.
assumptions: Other data stores in the system contain student-related information that can be correlated

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Assignment Data
description: Assignment files with student identifiers stored in DS1 could be accessed by unauthorized parties if the datastore is compromised, leading to disclosure of student submissions and personal information.
assumptions: Datastore has access controls that could potentially be bypassed or misconfigured

title: Excessive Data Collection for Assignment Storage
description: The flow collects student ID, course, and submission time alongside assignment files. While some data is necessary for grading, the minimality principle should be evaluated to ensure only strictly required personal data is stored.
assumptions: All three data elements (student ID, course, submission time) are being stored together with assignment files
uncertainty_note: Uncertain whether all data elements are strictly necessary for the grading function

title: Student Unawareness of Data Storage
description: Students may not be fully aware that their submission time and course information are being stored alongside their assignment files in the Assignment Store, beyond just the assignment content itself.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate all data elements being stored

title: Lack of Student Control Over Stored Data
description: Once assignments are submitted and stored in DS1, students have limited ability to control, modify, or delete their personal data (student ID, submission time) associated with their submissions.
assumptions: System does not provide mechanisms for students to manage their stored assignment metadata

title: Processing of identified teacher data
description: The system requests and processes identified data from the teacher during login (credentials, identity, course associations). This enables the system to identify and track the specific teacher making the request.
assumptions: Teacher authentication requires identification data to be transmitted

title: Linkability of teacher identity to review activities
description: The teacher's identity can be linked to their submission review activities, creating a profile of which teacher reviews which submissions and when. This enables tracking of teacher behavior patterns.
assumptions: System logs associate teacher identity with their review actions

title: Disclosure of teacher credentials during login
description: Teacher authentication credentials (username, password, tokens) could be disclosed during transmission from the teacher to the Grades Portal Web App, potentially through interception or logging.
assumptions: Credentials are transmitted over the network during login

title: Teacher unawareness of data collection scope
description: The teacher may not be fully aware of what data is being collected during login and submission queue requests (e.g., IP address, device information, timestamps, course associations).
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate all data collection practices

title: Linkability of student submissions to identities
description: The data flow contains student names paired with work content and submission times. If intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties, this data could be used to link specific students to their academic submissions, potentially revealing patterns about individual students' work habits and performance.
assumptions: Data is transmitted without adequate encryption or access controls

title: Direct identifiability of students in submission data
description: Student names are explicitly included in the data flow to teachers. Unauthorized access to this flow would directly reveal student identities along with their academic work, violating student privacy.
assumptions: Access controls may not properly restrict who can view this data flow

title: Unauthorized disclosure of student academic data
description: Student submissions, names, and submission times could be disclosed to unauthorized parties (e.g., other teachers, students, external entities) if the data flow is not properly secured during transmission or at the teacher endpoint.
assumptions: Transmission may lack encryption or endpoint security may be insufficient

title: Aggregation of student submission patterns
description: Multiple data flows over time could be aggregated to build comprehensive profiles of individual students' submission patterns, work quality trends, and academic performance, potentially revealing sensitive information beyond what was intended to be shared.
assumptions: Historical data is retained and accessible for aggregation

title: Student unawareness of data sharing with teachers
description: Students may not be fully aware that their submissions, names, and submission times are being transmitted to and displayed for teachers through this portal, or what specific data elements are included in this flow.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain this data flow

title: Linkability of grade records to student profiles
description: Student ID and grader ID in the grade submission can be linked to other data about the same student (e.g., other assignments, attendance, performance history) or teacher (grading patterns, other students graded), enabling comprehensive profiling.
assumptions: System maintains multiple data stores with student and teacher information that can be cross-referenced

title: Direct identifiability of students and teachers
description: Student ID and grader ID directly identify specific individuals in the grade submission, making this personally identifiable information (PII) that requires protection.
assumptions: Student ID and grader ID are unique identifiers that can be mapped to real individuals

title: Non-repudiation of grade submission
description: Without proper audit logging, a teacher could deny having submitted a particular grade or feedback, creating accountability issues and potential disputes.
assumptions: System may not maintain immutable audit trails of all grade submissions

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grades and feedback
description: Grades and written feedback are sensitive information that could be intercepted during transmission from teacher to the web application if not properly encrypted.
assumptions: Data transmission may not use end-to-end encryption or could be vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks

title: Data aggregation revealing patterns
description: Multiple grade submissions can be aggregated to reveal patterns about student performance over time, teacher grading tendencies, or comparative performance across students.
assumptions: System stores historical grade data that can be queried and combined

title: Lack of student control over grade data
description: Students have no control over what grade information is submitted by teachers, how it's stored, or who can access it once submitted to the system.
assumptions: Students cannot modify, delete, or restrict access to grades once teachers submit them

title: Processing of identified student data
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes personally identifiable student information when handling grade requests. The student's identity is explicitly linked to their academic records during this flow.
assumptions: Student authentication is required to access grades

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grades
description: Student grades and feedback could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission or processing. Grade data is highly sensitive and protected under educational privacy regulations.
assumptions: Grades contain sensitive academic performance information

title: Non-compliance with educational privacy regulations
description: The flow may not comply with FERPA or other educational privacy regulations governing student record access and disclosure. Proper authorization and audit mechanisms may be insufficient.
assumptions: Educational institution is subject to FERPA or similar regulations
uncertainty_note: Regulatory framework may vary by jurisdiction

title: Student unawareness of data processing
description: Students may not be fully aware of what data is collected, how long it's retained, or with whom it might be shared when requesting grades and feedback.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not be prominently displayed during grade access

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grades and feedback
description: If the Grades Portal Web App is compromised or has insufficient access controls, student grades and teacher feedback could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission or storage.
assumptions: Portal has authentication and authorization mechanisms in place

title: Academic profile aggregation
description: Grades and feedback data transmitted to students over time could be aggregated to build comprehensive academic profiles, potentially revealing patterns about student performance, learning difficulties, or behavioral trends.
assumptions: Portal retains historical grade data and access logs

title: Student unawareness of data usage
description: Students may not be fully aware of how their grades and feedback data are being stored, retained, or potentially shared with third parties (e.g., analytics providers, institutional researchers).
assumptions: Privacy policy exists but may not be prominently displayed or understood

title: Linkability of parent login to child grade data
description: Parent's authentication credentials and grade request can be linked to identify which parent is accessing which child's grades, potentially revealing family relationships and access patterns.
assumptions: System maintains parent-child account linkage

title: Identifiability of parent and child through login
description: Parent login credentials and child account linkage enable identification of both parent and child, exposing their identities to the system.
assumptions: Parent authentication uses identifiable credentials

title: Disclosure of grades during transmission
description: Child's grades transmitted from web app to parent could be intercepted if connection is not properly secured (e.g., missing TLS/encryption).
assumptions: Data transmitted over network between P1 and EE2

title: Non-repudiation of grade access request
description: Parent could deny having requested grades if system lacks proper audit logging of access requests and authentication events.
assumptions: Audit logging may be incomplete or absent

title: Data aggregation from repeated grade requests
description: Multiple grade access requests over time could be aggregated to build profiles of parent engagement patterns or child academic performance trends.
assumptions: System logs access history

title: Unawareness of metadata collection
description: Parent may be unaware of what metadata (timestamps, IP addresses, device info) is collected during login and grade request process.
assumptions: Privacy policy may not clearly disclose metadata collection

title: Linkability of parent identity to child's academic data
description: The flow enables linking the parent's identity with their child's grades, feedback, and submission history, creating a persistent association between parent and child academic records that could be used for profiling or tracking.
assumptions: Parent authentication is in place; data is intended for authorized parent only

title: Disclosure of sensitive educational data to parent
description: Grades, feedback, and submission history constitute sensitive educational data being disclosed to the parent. While typically authorized, improper access controls could allow unauthorized parents to view another child's data.
assumptions: Parent authorization verification is implemented; FERPA/GDPR compliance requirements apply

title: Aggregation of multiple data types reveals comprehensive academic profile
description: Combining grades, feedback, and submission history in a single flow creates a more complete academic profile than individual data points, potentially revealing patterns about the child's learning style, struggles, and performance trends.
assumptions: All three data types are transmitted together in this flow

title: Child unaware of data sharing with parent
description: The child (data subject) may not be aware that their academic data is being shared with their parent, particularly if the child is a minor or if consent mechanisms are not transparent.
assumptions: Child is a minor; consent/notification mechanisms may not be in place
uncertainty_note: Depends on child's age and jurisdiction-specific consent requirements

title: Potential non-compliance with educational data privacy regulations
description: Sharing educational data with parents may not comply with age-based consent requirements (e.g., FERPA, GDPR) if the system does not properly verify parent authorization or respect student privacy rights at certain ages.
assumptions: System operates in jurisdiction with educational data privacy laws; parent verification may be incomplete
uncertainty_note: Specific compliance depends on jurisdiction and implementation details

title: Direct Identifiers in Account Management
description: Administrator transmits names and email addresses when creating/modifying accounts, enabling direct identification of students and parents.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over network without additional anonymization

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Personal Data
description: Names, emails, roles, and parent-child relationships could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission to the Grades Portal.
assumptions: Network transmission may not be fully secured or monitored

title: Linkability of Account Data to Other Records
description: Account creation/modification data (names, emails, relationships) can be linked to other student/parent data in the system, creating comprehensive profiles.
assumptions: System maintains multiple data stores with overlapping identifiers

title: Non-repudiation of Administrator Actions
description: If account modifications are not properly logged, administrators could deny creating, modifying, or disabling accounts and parent-child links.
assumptions: Audit logging may be incomplete or absent

title: Data Aggregation Revealing Family Structures
description: Multiple account modifications with parent-child relationships could be aggregated to reveal family structures and relationships beyond intended scope.
assumptions: Multiple data points can be correlated across time

title: Unawareness of Data Processing
description: Parents and students may not be aware when their accounts are being created, modified, or disabled, or what data is being processed.
assumptions: Notification mechanisms may not be in place

title: Non-compliance with Privacy Regulations
description: Processing of personal data (names, emails, relationships) may not comply with FERPA, GDPR, or other applicable privacy regulations if proper consent and safeguards are not in place.
assumptions: Regulatory compliance measures may be incomplete
uncertainty_note: Specific regulatory requirements depend on jurisdiction and implementation details

title: Linkability of parent-child relationships
description: The grading service writes parent-child relationship links to the account directory, creating linkability between family members' accounts. This enables correlation of student and parent data across the system.
assumptions: Parent-child relationship data is stored in a way that can be queried and linked

title: Identifiability of account records
description: Account records written by the grading service contain personally identifiable information about students and parents, making individuals identifiable within the account directory.
assumptions: Account records contain PII such as names, IDs, or other identifying information

title: Disclosure of sensitive account data
description: Account records and parent-child relationship links written to the account directory could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through data store access controls or breaches.
assumptions: Data store has access control mechanisms that could be bypassed or misconfigured

title: Data aggregation in account directory
description: The account directory aggregates account records and relationship links from the grading service, potentially enabling inference of additional sensitive information through data combination.
assumptions: Multiple data sources write to the same account directory, enabling cross-referencing

title: Unawareness of data processing
description: Students and parents may not be aware that their account records and relationship links are being written to the account directory by the grading service.
assumptions: Privacy notices do not clearly communicate this data flow

title: Full data disclosure to third-party cloud provider
description: Nightly backup transfers complete grade records, assignments, and account directory to external cloud hosting provider. This represents explicit data disclosure across system boundary. Question whether 'full' records are necessary or if minimization could be applied (e.g., excluding sensitive fields, using pseudonymization).
assumptions: Cloud hosting provider is a legitimate third-party service with appropriate security controls in place

title: Student unawareness of third-party data replication
description: Students may not be aware that their grade records, assignments, and account information are being replicated to a third-party cloud hosting provider as part of backup operations. This affects transparency and informed consent.
assumptions: Privacy policy may not explicitly detail backup replication to third-party providers

title: Loss of control over student data at cloud provider
description: Once data is transferred to the cloud hosting provider, the institution loses direct control over how the data is stored, accessed, and protected. The cloud provider's security practices, sub-contractors, and compliance with privacy regulations are outside the institution's direct oversight.
assumptions: Cloud provider operates under standard commercial terms with limited institutional oversight

title: Linkability of student data across cloud provider's ecosystem
description: Cloud hosting provider may link student grade records and account information with other data they hold (from other institutions, services, or sources), potentially creating comprehensive profiles that exceed the original purpose of backup/replication.
assumptions: Cloud provider may aggregate data from multiple clients or services
uncertainty_note: Depends on cloud provider's data practices and contractual restrictions

title: Grade records linkable to student identities
description: Grade records in DS2 contain student identifiers that could be linked across different contexts (e.g., linking grades to student profiles, attendance records, or other systems), potentially revealing sensitive patterns about individual students.
assumptions: Grade records contain student identifiers and are accessed by the grading service for multiple view types

title: Student identities exposed through grade data access
description: When P2 reads grade records from DS2, student identifying information could be exposed to unauthorized parties or logged inappropriately, especially if access controls are not properly implemented.
assumptions: Grade records contain PII and the grading service may not have granular access controls

title: Unauthorized disclosure of grade information
description: Grade records are sensitive PII. If the grading service (P2) does not properly restrict access, grade information could be disclosed to unauthorized parties (e.g., wrong students viewing other students' grades, or external unauthorized access).
assumptions: Grade data is sensitive and requires strict access control; service may have insufficient authorization checks

title: Grade data aggregation reveals sensitive patterns
description: The grading service aggregates grade records to build views for students, parents, and teachers. This aggregation could reveal patterns or inferences about students that were not intended to be disclosed (e.g., performance trends, comparisons).
assumptions: Multiple grade records are aggregated to create views; aggregation may reveal more than individual records

title: Students/parents unaware of grade data processing
description: Students and parents may not be aware of how their grade data is being accessed, processed, and shared by the grading service, including what views are created and who can access them.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain grade data processing activities

title: Limited control over grade data access and use
description: Students and parents may have limited ability to control how their grade information is accessed by the grading service, what views are created, or who can see their grades beyond the intended audience.
assumptions: Data subjects may not have granular consent or control mechanisms for grade data processing
